messages.subject: Using the "logit" link in rstanarm
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to fit my data using a logit link in rstanarm. It appears to work well with categorical variables but fail to predict continuous predictor variables (yellow highlighted in results). How can I sort this out?

Also is it possible to specify the initial predictor coefficient values. I wonder whether it is possible that with rstanarm.

                      seed = 123,

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using the "logit" link in rstanarm
parts:
On Sunday, October 23, 2016 at 1:28:47 PM UTC-4, malai...@gmail.com wrote:
I am trying to fit my data using a logit link in rstanarm. It appears to work well with categorical variables but fail to predict continuous predictor variables (yellow highlighted in results). How can I sort this out?

I think you mean the marginal posterior distributions in yellow are not what you expected. But your prior mean was zero, so I don't know what is the basis for that. It is quite possible that your continuous predictors are in units that such that a one-unit change has a negligible effect on the predictions, in which case you should change the units.

But the big thing is that you should pretty much always specify the QR = TRUE argument with stan_glm unless you have informative priors about the mean or only one predictor. It is quite possible that these results that use the default of QR = FALSE are not reliable.
Also is it possible to specify the initial predictor coefficient values. I wonder whether it is possible that with rstanarm.

Don't worry about that.

Ben

parts:
The summary method should have a "digits" argument. Alternatively you can extract the draws using as.matrix and then do your own summary with as many digits as you want.

Also, a small correction to Ben's previous post: you should set normal(0,1) manually if using QR=TRUE. The default for coefficients actually results in normal(0,2.5) not standard normal.

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Using the "logit" link in rstanarm
parts:
If you just want to see the correlations between all the predictors then you can just use the regular cor function in R, which I believe works for a matrix or a data frame. 

Also if you set the QR argument to true when estimating your model, as Ben recommended, then the predictor matrix actually used to fit the model will have no correlations between any predictors by design. This is one reason why the QR option is nice. If you don't use QR then the correlations will be whatever cor says they are. 

Hope that helps,

Jonah

On Monday, October 24, 2016 at 8:56:47 AM UTC-4, malai...@gmail.com wrote:
One more question, I would like to get the result estimates in three decimal points. How can I assign that in my script?

This can be done by passing the digits argument, but it would be better to divide the variables by 1000 before estimating the model. The third decimal place of the posterior median is not estimated with any genuine accuracy.
